clue.text: Too much where entrenched soldiers were made to go?

definitions.text: where entrenched soldiers were made to go?

blocks.note: first meaning: excessive, exaggerated beyond what is reasonable

blocks.clueFragment: where entrenched soldiers were made to go?
blocks.note: second meaning: First World War troops were ordered up out of the trench and over its parapet to attack

explanation.surface: A complaint that too much was asked of soldiers in the trenches.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase literally described climbing over the trench parapet into no man's land in the First World War; the question mark flags the historical, literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for something excessive or outrageous comes from that wartime order to charge.

clue.text: Over 50 in substantial European force

indicators.note: one piece placed in another means it sits inside that word's letters

blocks.note: O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over
substantial means big
L is the Roman numeral for 50
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A substantial European military force of over fifty units.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' reads as 'more than' beside 50, but it is the cricket over; the 50 goes inside the word for substantial.
explanation.definitionFit: To oblige someone is to compel or force them to do something, as in 'obliged to resign'.

clue.text: Wayward customer ran through stores

indicators.note: the phrase stores, that is holds within it, the letters that are wanted

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of customer, all of ran, and the start of through

explanation.surface: An unruly shopper dashing between the aisles of a store.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant means straying from the proper course, which is what wayward behaviour does.

clue.text: One disappearing act changed after tricky hitches here

indicators.note: something changed has been altered, so the letters of act are rearranged
tricky suggests something twisted and complicated, so those letters are jumbled
after tells us which piece comes second when the parts are joined

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A magician's vanishing act gets reworked after some awkward hitches on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface 'disappearing act' runs across the definition and the wordplay; the definition is only 'One disappearing'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Alice's Adventures in Wonderland the grinning cat famously vanishes, leaving only its grin behind.

clue.text: Passing border in record time, heading for Lusaka

indicators.note: the border is placed in the other words, sitting inside their letters
a heading is what stands at the top, so only the opening letter of the place is used

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a hem is the border of a piece of cloth
an era is a period of time
the opening letter of Lusaka

explanation.surface: A traveller crossing a border in record time on the way to Lusaka, capital of Zambia.
explanation.walkthrough: The border sits between the record and the time, rather than inside either one alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral things are fleeting and short-lived, just as a passing fancy lasts only a moment.

clue.text: Middle of grotto in which walker, oddly, is nestling

indicators.note: only the central letters of the word are wanted
oddly means taking the letters in odd-numbered positions
in which means the second piece is put inside the first

blocks.note: the two central letters of grotto
the first, third and fifth letters of walker

explanation.surface: A hiker tucked away in the heart of a cave, oddly snug there.
explanation.walkthrough: WLE goes between O and T: O(WLE)T. 'Nestling' looks like a verb, but here it is the noun for a young bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A nestling is a chick too young to leave the nest, and an owlet is a baby owl.

clue.text: See 19
A very English Mass with song and prayer

blocks.note: taken as written
V is the abbreviation for very
E is the abbreviation for English
M is the symbol for mass in physics
an aria is a solo song in an opera; with just joins it on

explanation.surface: A description of a very English church Mass with hymns and prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' tempts as a church service, but here it is just M, the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hail Mary, a Catholic prayer to the Virgin, is called Ave Maria in Latin.

clue.text: Vast area sweetheart tours with male

indicators.note: to tour something is to go all round it, so the sweetheart surrounds the rest

blocks.note: a lass is a girlfriend or sweetheart
and means with, along with
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A girlfriend touring a huge region with her male partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a mere link, but it supplies letters of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A landmass is a large continuous expanse of land, such as a continent.

clue.text: Ridicule swimmer thus leading course

blocks.note: to mock is to ridicule
a turtle is a sea creature that swims
so means thus, in this way
up means ahead, as in a team up by two goals

explanation.surface: Someone jeering at the swimmer who is leading the race course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks like a racecourse, but it is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mock turtle soup is a Victorian dish made with calf's head to imitate real turtle soup, served as a course.

clue.text: Mammoth damaged leg crossing a river

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged
to cross something here is to straddle it, so the rearranged letters go around the rest

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A woolly mammoth with an injured leg wading across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mammoth' reads as the prehistoric animal, but it is an adjective meaning huge.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, mammoth means enormous, a synonym of large.

clue.text: Female bringing in own ecstasy: party time?

indicators.note: bringing something in takes it inside, so the female word holds the others

blocks.note: a hen is a female bird
to own can mean to admit or allow, as in owning that something is true
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A woman who brings her own drugs along to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: To own up is to admit, hence allow. The question mark marks the definition as an example: Halloween is one time for parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Halloween on 31 October is a night of costume parties, so it is an instance of a party time.

clue.text: Leaving minus Oscar bad actor checked material

indicators.note: minus means take away, so the named letter is removed

blocks.note: leaving means going
Oscar is the NATO alphabet code word for O
a ham is an over-the-top, bad actor

explanation.surface: A poor actor quitting without an Oscar, his costume of checked fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop O from GOING to leave GING, then add HAM. 'Oscar' tempts as the film award; here it is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Gingham is a cotton fabric woven in a pattern of small checks, as on picnic tablecloths.

clue.text: Set sights and capture first-rate spy boss

blocks.note: to take is to capture
A1 means first-rate, written with the letter I standing for the digit 1
M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A spy chief setting his sights on capturing a top agent.
explanation.walkthrough: AI for first-rate is a crossword convention for A1, with I in place of the 1.
explanation.definitionFit: To set your sights on a target and to take aim at it are equivalent idioms for pointing a weapon.

clue.text: Caution: stars exploding in space science

indicators.note: something exploding is blown apart, so these letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning in astronomy class that stars may explode.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronautics is the science and technology of travel beyond Earth's atmosphere.

clue.text: Clubs in midday match without serious competition

indicators.note: the clubs symbol is put in the other word, sitting inside it

blocks.note: noon is midday
C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: Golf clubs used in a midday match against weak opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' suggests golf, but it is the card suit; a Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A no contest is a one-sided affair where one side wins easily, with no real rivalry.

clue.text: Like mummy's fragrance in sea around Cyprus?

indicators.note: the fragrance is placed in the sea, so it sits inside those letters

blocks.note: Cyprus lies in the eastern Mediterranean, abbreviated E Med
balm is a sweet-smelling ointment or fragrance

explanation.surface: Mother's perfume, bought in the waters around Cyprus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mummy' looks like a mother, but it is an Egyptian mummy; the 's stands for is. BALM goes inside E MED.
explanation.definitionFit: A mummy is a body preserved by embalming, treated with resins and spices.

clue.text: Knight visiting Capitol strangely eschewing Congress?

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside a building, so the knight goes into the other word
strangely means in an odd way, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A knight touring the US Capitol oddly avoids the Congress that sits there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' points to the US legislature in the Capitol, but here it means sexual intercourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A platonic relationship is affectionate but not sexual, so it avoids congress in its old sense of intercourse.

clue.text: Host summit in Scots isle with one large town

indicators.note: the summit is put in the isle, inside its letters

blocks.note: Mull is an island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland
the tip is the top or summit
I is the Roman numeral for one; with just joins it on
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: Planning to host a summit on a Scottish island alongside a big town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning a great number.
explanation.definitionFit: A host of things is a great many of them, and multiplicity likewise means a large number or variety.

clue.text: Eccentric no longer keen on Pink Floyd masterpiece?

blocks.note: to go off something is to stop liking it
Pink Floyd's 1979 rock opera album

explanation.surface: An oddball who has gone off a classic Pink Floyd album.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that calling the album a masterpiece is the setter's opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Off the wall is an informal idiom for bizarre or unconventional, just as eccentric means odd.

clue.text: Look good on knight's arm

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a lance is the long spear a mounted knight carried

explanation.surface: Admiring how fine the armour looks on a knight's arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arm' suggests a limb, but here it is a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A glance is a quick look, so the noun look in the sense of a brief glimpse fits it.

clue.text: An ass making port in Belgium

blocks.note: taken as written
a twerp is a silly person, an ass

explanation.surface: A donkey arriving at a Belgian harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ass' tempts as the animal; it means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp, on the Scheldt river, is one of Europe's biggest seaports, in northern Belgium.

clue.text: Left in place old Disney character

indicators.note: the letter for left is placed in the following word, sitting inside it

blocks.note: to put something is to place it
L is the abbreviation for left
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An old Disney character left in his place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' reads as a noun, but it is the verb meaning to set down.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluto is Mickey Mouse's pet dog in Disney cartoons, first appearing in 1930.

clue.text: Dancing nude almost felt necessary

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and fall into a new order
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
felt with its final letter removed

explanation.surface: A dancer who felt that dancing naked was almost obligatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Needful is an old-fashioned word for required, so it is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Perhaps bonsai blossom in island's cut

indicators.note: the other word is cut, sliced open so the preceding letters fit inside

blocks.note: to blossom is to develop or mature
taken as written
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A tiny tree in blossom being pruned on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is: IN + I cuts into MATURE after its first letter, M(IN I)ATURE. 'Perhaps' marks bonsai as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonsai is a tree grown in tiny form, an example of a miniature, something made on a small scale.

clue.text: Regularly seen around in Dunnet Forest

indicators.note: the letters can be seen sitting in plain view inside the phrase
turned around means the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of Dunnet and the start of Forest

explanation.surface: A walker who is often spotted in Dunnet Forest, a woodland in Caithness at the far north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something often means doing it frequently, so regularly is a close synonym.

clue.text: First to defeat brilliant swimmer

indicators.note: first to means only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: the opening letter of defeat
ace means excellent or brilliant

explanation.surface: An outstanding swimmer being the first to beat the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' looks like a person in a race, but it is a fish, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: The dace is a small freshwater fish of the carp family, so it is a swimmer.

clue.text: Spokesperson opening with dramatic work

blocks.note: a mouth is an opening, as of a cave or river
a piece is a play or other theatrical work

explanation.surface: A spokesperson opening a speech with a theatrical performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouthpiece is someone who speaks on behalf of another, such as a press officer.
